newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo in generic drug deal with Novopharm.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo in generic drug deal with Novopharm.

text.p: British drugs company Glaxo Wellcome Plc said on Thursday its U.S. unit Glaxo Wellcome Inc. had signed a licensing agreement allowing NovoPharm Inc. to market a generic form of Glaxo's ulcer treatment Zantac.

Under the terms of the deal, Novopharm will be able to market its generic treatment 16 days earlier than other manufacturers, a Glaxo spokesman said. In return, Glaxo will receive payments from Novopharm.
The spokesman said Glaxo had also decided not to pursue an appeal of patent infringement litigation. The U.S. Court of Appeals recently ruled in Novopharm's favour in the case.
Glaxo had tried to prevent Novopharm marketing its generic form of Zantac but a court said Novopharm could market the drug from mid-July.
Novopharm will be able to market the generic drug from July 10, Glaxo said.
Zantac, the best-selling drug upon which Glaxo built its international fortune, at one time accounted for more than half of the company's sales.
The company warned in March it faced two lean years after the Zantac patent expiry.
